theme-full: The strongest piece. Intro, A, B, A' and coda with Zoo's motif in every section and Badger's figure as the bookends. The voicings are audited: no held semitone or minor-ninth rubs outside the deliberate A7(b9) colour. It passes the standalone profile. Risks a producer may hear, unverified by ear: the FM tine piano and the synth brass are our own synthesis and may read slightly synthetic where exposed (the A' hits). The stop-time bar before B (about 1 s of near silence at 22.5 s) is meant as a late-night band stop but could feel like a dropout. The VSCO string swells in B are soft-attack samples and may smear the faster chord changes.
theme-15s: The same bars, recut: the motif three times and Badger twice in 15 s. That much repetition is the point of a brand stamp, but it is a lot. The button lands at 12.0-12.6 s and the tail is clean by 15.0 s.
theme-5s: The band plays the motif in unison from the first sample (no pickup), so it starts hard. SHOW lands at 1.2 s and Badger's button at 2.4/3.0 s, and it decays under -60 dBFS by 5.0 s. It is warm and dark (2-5 kHz well under pink), as intended for a sting under picture. The kick and bass carry a lot of the weight.
intro-sting-show: Locked to the ShowSting frames: SHOW on frame 30 and Badger's D on frame 58, within a few ms of humanising. The motif runs faster here (about 138 BPM) than in the theme so it fits before the ampersand hit. The music is out before the 4.0 s hard cut. The hum warning is a false positive from short, bass-heavy material (A1/D2 partials near 55-60 Hz); there is no mains hum in any source.
intro-sting-zoora: A harp and string shimmer rises from frame 6, and the lydian motif on celesta and vibes lands on the logo hit (frame 54) with an F-add9 bloom. Two celesta notes sit under the wordmark and tag (frames 70 and 78), and it fades with the picture. It is the most cinematic cue and quite dark (harshness -8.9). The MuseScore celesta is the weakest sample in it. Listen for whether the reversed piano bloom reads as intended or as a swoosh.
bumper-rekt-meter: The meter fills (taps, rising pizzicato and air), then the motif's tail A, Ab, F falls with band stabs and a crash. The idea reads: the gauge rises and the price drops. The 1.2 s fill may feel rushed at 100 BPM; a 3.6 s version with a two-beat fill is an easy change.
bumper-red-flag: Deadpan: the motif head (D D A) on pizzicato and piano, a beat and a half of nothing, then Badger's Eb-D in the low register with dry ticks. It works only if the rest is long enough to read as a pause rather than a mistake; I believe it is, but this one needs an ear. There is room after 2.6 s for the owner's real dog sound.
bumper-one-fix: The major motif (D D A G# F#) on vibes and piano, then a rim click and a harp lift into D6/9: helpful and resolved without cheer. It is light; the bass is kept soft after the first mix read bottom-heavy.
bumper-scam-of-the-week: Low and sly: the motif in piano octaves and pizzicato over a cymbal scrape. It lands unresolved on Bb7(b9), and a vibes tritone glint (E then Bb) follows. It is the most character-driven bumper and leans towards the noir spy idiom; I kept the minor-major Bond chord out on purpose.
bumper-developing: A news alert, not an alarm: three beats of rising 16th ticker (pulse, muted piano, hats) under a tremolo swell. The motif head then lands on Dsus4(add9) and stays open. No sirens, no risers to white noise.
bumper-correction: Sober: a reversed piano swell (the rewind) runs straight into the motif played backwards, calm, resolving to D minor. It is the darkest bumper (harshness -8.6). Its piano voicings were thinned and 700 Hz cut after the first render read boxy. It is normalised to the same -16 LUFS-I as the others, so check that it does not feel louder than its mood.
endscreen-bed: Six bars of light groove, a turnaround, then the motif lands on D minor at 18.0 s and rings out to exactly 20.0 s. It is a bed level (-26 LUFS-S) with a deep voice pocket for Zoo's call to action. Played without a voice-over it will feel quiet: raise it 6-8 dB.
bed-show-neutral: D dorian over a pedal: EP, bass, soft kick, cross-stick and shaker; the motif on soft vibes from bar 8 and a quiet string pad in bars 16-21. The loop is seamless (seam ratio well under 1). The level-step warning is the downbeat at the loop start versus the last 100 ms of bar 24, not a click. The 8-16 kHz floor warning is the continuous shaker, not hiss. The EP carries this bed, so if it sounds synthetic, this bed suffers most.
bed-show-tension: A muted 3-3-2 pulse, low strings with an Eb neighbour, a half-time kit with ticking hats, and the motif low on piano every 8 bars. It is the bed with the most low end; the sub and bass were pulled down after the first mix read +8 dB at 63 Hz. The hum warning is a false positive (sustained D/A bass partials).
bed-show-light: Swung pizzicato, a two-feel bass and soft taps and hats, with the major motif on vibes every 8 bars (the lydian B is the wink). Anticipation chords cross every 8-bar line so the loop flows. Some pizzicato-arpeggio weight sits around 500 Hz; it passes but is the busiest show bed in the voice's body range.
bed-story-curious: F lydian: a harp ostinato an octave up, high bowed-vibes sustains and the motif augmented on celesta; kalimba and pizzicato from bar 8, marimba from 16. The first mix had a +9 dB hump at 250-1000 Hz that would have masked narration; moving the harp up an octave and a bus scoop fixed it (mud now within limits). It stays warm and dark above 2 kHz, which helps the voice but may read soft on its own.
bed-story-tension: A celli ostinato with phrygian Eb neighbours, a woodblock clock and low piano octaves; the pulse, violas tremolo and the motif's tail from bar 8; high violins and tom rolls from bar 16. The short Eb-over-D rubs are the intended tension. It passes with a modest voice pocket.
bed-story-ominous: Drones, a frame-drum heartbeat, low piano octaves with the D-Ab tritone, bowed-vibes dissonances (Eb5 over the D drone is a deliberate minor ninth, quiet) and the motif four times slower on low piano. It is the most uncomfortable bed by design. Check on a phone speaker that the heartbeat and drones do not vanish (they live under 150 Hz).
bed-story-resolve: D major: piano arpeggios an octave up, the major motif on vibes and violins, strings, a soft kick and shaker from bar 8, and a harp lift at bar 16. It is warm and open; the A7sus4 at the loop end leads back to D. Its true peak sits far under the ceiling because it is soft, sustained material.
